payload.summary: unified-agent CHEF falsely reports send_telegram parser-failure, fails to publish the dish, and pollutes channel=market with debug test fragments.
payload.evidence: intraday 08:20 UTC cycle (agentId af9b608dd2dd004f6): chef completed full TNB analysis but reported 'send_telegram gateway parser error on messages >20 chars' and did NOT publish. RAW get_unreviewed_market_messages showed NO real dish since id=702 (06:22) — only 7 chef debug fragments id703-709 ('Test message','x','NVL','NVL tang','NVL tang 688 do tai cau','NVL vang giam','NVL vang') sent 08:22-08:25Z to channel=market. send_telegram is HEALTHY (those fragments AND the prior long id=702 dish landed fine). Dispatcher completed the publish itself -> MARKET id=710 08:28:18Z.
payload.recurrence: 2nd chef publish-reliability flow_bug (prior: cwk-chef-eod-marker). 2+ same-module -> recurring-bug-escalation: PM blocks, calls Architect.
payload.recommended_fix: chef.md publish step hardening: (1) after send_telegram(channel=market) the chef MUST RAW-verify its own publish by message id via get_unreviewed_market_messages before declaring success OR failure — never infer failure from an ambiguous tool response; (2) NEVER emit debug/test fragments to channel=market — diagnostics go to channel=bug only; (3) on a genuine publish error, route to channel=bug + emit flow_bug, do not silently abandon the dish. Root cause likely a brittle error-handling branch that misreads a non-error response as a parser failure.
